n01: You can build an API in an afternoon. But can you explain it out loud, in an interview, without freezing?
n02: Most engineers know the material. What breaks is the speaking. The fillers, the tense slips, the answer with no shape.
n03: Meet Bolo. A speaking coach for engineers, built on Gnani AI's voice models.
n04: You speak for up to thirty seconds. Gnani Prisma transcribes you, jargon and Hinglish included.
n05: Bolo checks every word, your pace and your structure. Then Gnani Timbre speaks the one fix that matters.
n06: Every topic is a ladder. Read it. Say it back from memory. Build your own version. Then speak freely.
n07: Here, an interviewer asks about caching. First try, the way most of us really talk.
n08: Every slip is marked on your own sentence. Struck in red, fixed in green.
n09: You see your pace, the fillers, and whether your answer had a hook, a problem, an action and a result.
n10: Then a stronger version of your own answer, read aloud by Timbre.
n11: Try again. Same question, a better answer. And the score climbs.
n12: One tap turns your progress into a card you can share.
n13: There are four tracks. Tech talks, everyday grammar, talking to camera like a creator, and live voice conversations for stand-ups and HR rounds.
n14: Built solo, on Gnani Prisma and Timbre. And it is live today.
n15: Bolo. Speak up. Get better every try.
n16: Grammar practice shows the rule in plain words after every try.
n17: In conversation mode, the coach plays your manager or your interviewer, replies by voice, and corrects one thing at a time.
n18: Under the hood, Prisma gets the topic and key terms, so words like JSON and Redis come out right. And Timbre gives the coach a warm Indian English voice.
n19: It is made for students facing placements, and for developers who want to sound as good as their code.
n20: And you are not limited to our topics. Type anything, like how UPI payments work, and Bolo writes a passage for it. You learn the topic, and how to explain it.
n21: Type any topic, and Bolo writes the passage for you.
